items.caseName: Mrinal Harsh Vardhan v. Hynite Farms Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
items.coram: Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member), Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
items.headline: Lawyer's polite email asking NCLT to upload its order was no misconduct; adverse remarks expunged
items.text: The NCLT had criticised a lawyer for emailing its Court Master about an order that had not been uploaded for about 18 days, though it was needed to implement an approved resolution plan. The NCLAT found the email justified and mildly worded, called the remarks uncalled for and ordered them struck off, while clarifying that the ruling gives no advantage in separate contempt proceedings.

items.caseName: Beacon Trusteeship Limited v. Vatika IT Parks Private Limited
items.coram: Manni Shankariah Shanmuga Sundaram (Judicial Member), Reena Sinha Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: Vatika IT Parks admitted into insolvency over ₹233.75 crore debenture default
items.text: The debenture trustee for ARCIL sought insolvency after Vatika IT Parks failed to redeem optionally convertible debentures when the put option was exercised in January 2025. Rejecting the plea that the debentures had already become compulsorily convertible, the Tribunal held that a conversion notice alone does not complete conversion without the statutory steps, so the debentures remained debt; it admitted the petition, appointed an IRP and declared a moratorium.

items.caseName: Vivek Khanna & Ors. v. Gaurav Katiyar
items.caseNo: I.A. 843 ND 2025 in C.P. IB 284 (PB) of 2021
items.coram: Mahendra Khandelwal (Judicial Member), Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Suspicion of proxy claims and family ties not enough to throw creditors out of CoC
items.text: Twenty homebuyers in the Spaze Towers insolvency sought to exclude seven creditors as alleged proxies of the suspended management and asked for a forensic audit. The Tribunal dismissed the plea, holding that payment discrepancies, shared addresses and family links did not prove ineligibility and that a resolution professional cannot conclusively decide fraud or benami questions.

items.caseName: Vivek Khanna & Ors. v. Gaurav Katiyar
items.caseNo: I.A. 844 ND 2025 in C.P. IB 284 (PB) of 2021
items.coram: Mahendra Khandelwal (Judicial Member), Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Homebuyers cannot demand other creditors' account statements on mere suspicion
items.text: In a companion application, the same Spaze Arrow homebuyers sought separate representation, a fresh audit, creditor-wise disclosures and ₹23 crore from the sale of the debtor's old office. The Tribunal held the insolvency covers the whole company, refused repeat audits and separate representation, and gave no creditor exclusive rights to sale proceeds.

items.caseName: Srinivasan PR (Liquidator) in the matter of Asten Realtors Private Limited
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member), Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Highest bidder gets no vested right in liquidation auction before sale is completed
items.text: After the highest bidder in an e-auction failed to pay the balance, the liquidator sought approval to sell the Asten Aurum Woods project privately to a homebuyer consortium for ₹4.96 crore. Relying on Supreme Court precedent and the auction notice's reservation clause, the Tribunal held the bidder had no enforceable right, approved the course taken and upheld refund of its earnest money with interest.

items.caseName: Cornell University v. Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (International Taxation)
items.coram: Beena Pillai (Judicial Member), Makarand Vasant Mahadeokar (Accountant Member)
items.headline: Cornell's ₹17.23 crore from online executive courses for Indians not taxable as fees for included services
items.text: The Assessing Officer had treated Cornell's AY 2022-23 receipts from digital courses taken by Indian students and corporate employees as technical or included services. The Tribunal held they fall within the teaching exclusion of Article 12(5)(c) of the India–USA DTAA even for non-degree professional courses, that payment of Equalisation Levy made no difference, and directed deletion of the addition.

items.caseName: Cornerstone OnDemand International Limited v. Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax (International Taxation)
items.coram: Beena Pillai (Judicial Member), Arun Khodpia (Accountant Member)
items.headline: Permanent establishment of a foreign company cannot be presumed from its Indian affiliate's work
items.text: The Revenue treated the Indian group entity of a UK software company as a dependent agent PE and attributed 30% of Indian sales, adding about ₹2.27 crore for AY 2020-21. The Tribunal held a PE cannot be assumed from the affiliate's activities and sent the PE and profit-attribution questions back to the Assessing Officer for a fresh, reasoned decision.

items.headline: Two PANs, before and after marriage: ITAT orders fresh check before ₹5.69 crore addition
items.text: The assessee, who held one PAN before marriage and another after, faced a ₹5.69 crore addition for AY 2018-19 on reopened assessment over bank transactions. Since the transactions may already have been disclosed in returns under the second PAN, the Tribunal sent the matter back for the Assessing Officer to verify returns and bank records under both PANs.

items.headline: Hyundai Creta, Alcazar and Tucson are SUVs for 22% compensation cess
items.text: A Hyundai dealer had paid compensation cess at 20% on the three models, while the Department said they met all the Entry 52B tests for SUVs, including engine size, length and ground clearance. Accepting the Department's appeal, the Tribunal held the vehicles attract 22% cess and restored the differential demand.

items.caseName: Smt. Parul v. Metro Heart Institute with Multi Speciality & Ors.
items.coram: Justice A.P. Sahi (President), Bharat Kumar Pandya (Member)
items.headline: Hospital and attending doctor liable for poor post-operative care; ₹20 lakh awarded
items.text: A 39-year-old patient died of pulmonary embolism the morning after a laparoscopic hernia operation at a Faridabad hospital in 2014. The Commission cleared the operating surgeon but held the hospital liable for inadequate post-operative care and the attending doctor for not investigating the embolism, awarding ₹15 lakh and ₹5 lakh respectively.

items.bench: Tamil Nadu Real Estate Appellate Tribunal, Chennai
items.caseName: M/s. Five Mount Villa Owners Welfare Association v. M/s. Bahri Estates Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
items.caseNo: Appeal No. 108 of 2026 and M.A. No. 278 of 2026
items.coram: Justice M. Duraiswamy (Chairperson), K. Babu (Judicial Member)
items.headline: Late handover does not restart three-year limitation for RERA compensation
items.text: A residents' association's 2022 compensation complaint over amenities and construction quality had been dismissed as time-barred. The Tribunal held Article 27 of the Limitation Act applies, that time ran from the October 2016 contractual possession date, and that later handover neither revived limitation nor attracted the COVID-19 extension; the appeal was dismissed.

items.headline: CCI clears KKR-backed Maybach Asia Holdings' acquisition of Sahrudaya Health Care
items.text: The Commission approved the acquisition of 100% of Sahrudaya Health Care Private Limited by Maybach Asia Holdings II Pte Ltd, a vehicle indirectly owned by KKR-managed funds. Sahrudaya and its subsidiaries run about 28 hospitals and units with some 4,800 beds across South and West India.
